title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typescript page numbered 101 of Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', in SGA 7 I (LNM 288, 1972). It appears to be a stray page in cote 136. The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on truncation functors for graded modules, which have nothing to do with this page.

Setting: A_K is an abelian variety over the fraction field K of a henselian DVR with residue characteristic p, and I is the inertia group. U = T_ℓ(A_K) is the ℓ-adic Tate module. V = U^I is the fixed part, which up to torsion is identified with the Tate module of the Néron model's special fibre. V^⊥ is the orthogonal of V for the Weil pairing between U and U' (the module of the dual abelian variety); by the orthogonality theorem of §2.5 it is the toric part W.

For ℓ ≠ p the argument runs as follows.
- Up to torsion, V = U^I is equivalent to saying that V^⊥ is generated by the elements gx − x. In any case gx − x lies in V^⊥ (9.2.1).
- Hence one can write g = 1 + u(g) (9.2.2), where u(g): U → V^⊥ vanishes on V. Equivalently u(g) ∈ Hom(U/V, V^⊥) ≅ (U/V)^∨ ⊗ V^⊥ (9.2.3).
- In the semi-stable case, V^⊥ ⊂ V, so u(g)u(h) = 0. Each g therefore acts as a transvection parallel to W, and composition corresponds to adding the u's.
- So the inertia action is entirely encoded by a group homomorphism I → (U/V)^∨ ⊗ V^⊥ (9.2.4). Since the target is a pro-ℓ abelian group, this map factors through the ℓ-part Z_ℓ(1) of tame inertia.

This is the first step towards the monodromy pairing of SGA 7 IX §10. That pairing is between the character groups of the toric parts of A and A', and it gives the description of the component groups of the Néron models.
errors: In the parenthesis '(u ∈ U, g ∈ I)', 'u' should be 'x', i.e. (x ∈ U, g ∈ I). This is a typo already present in the typescript.

'g ↦ u(g) est un homomorphisme de U dans V^⊥' is loosely phrased. For each g, u(g) is a homomorphism U → V^⊥. The map g ↦ u(g) is a group homomorphism only in the semi-stable case, as the page itself goes on to say.
Additivity under composition uses u(g)u(h) = 0. This follows from V^⊥ ⊂ V together with u vanishing on V. The page states the conclusion correctly, but this step is left implicit.

ideas.what: In the semi-stable case inertia acts unipotently on T_ℓ by transvections, (g−1)^2 = 0, and the action is encoded by a homomorphism I → Hom(U/V, V^⊥)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's semi-stable reduction / unipotent monodromy, the first step to the monodromy pairing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: Up to torsion, V^⊥ is generated by the elements gx − x, using the orthogonality theorem V^⊥ = W

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX (§9.2), misfiled among the 1976 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. All of its content is published and well known.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription faithfully reproduces '(u ∈ U, g ∈ I)'; the intended reading is (x ∈ U, g ∈ I).

The handwritten '419' at the bottom is the archive folio number, and '291' at the bottom left is a pencil mark. Neither is part of the text. The page is a stray typescript of SGA 7 Exp. IX, p. 101, not part of the manuscript notes on the neighbouring pages.
